doc.title: Jim Galloway interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Why he chose Toronto in the mid-1960s
summary: Canada welcomed educated immigrants, Toronto was British-influenced and near New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Oh I guess I did, it’s hard to recall. I obviously didn’t just wake up one morning and say well I’m going to Canada. I thought about it, and a lot of people have said why Toronto? And to put it all in perspective, in the mid-60s if you had a half decent education and if you were qualified in some sort of acceptable profession, and you see I had a degree from an art school, as a jazz musician they might not have wanted me, but I had this funny little piece of paper. Anyway in the mid-60s they welcomed people such as myself with open arms. It was more difficult, as it still is, to get entry into the United States. And Toronto seemed like a good spot because it was essentially still a strong British influence and it was real close to New York. So boom, Toronto it was.
